title: Lesson 58 - Efficient Fetch, Transform, and Save at the Solution Level
description: Provide guidance on the appropriate Data Mappers and Integration Procedures to use within an Omniscript to efficiently fetch, transform, and save data to meet specific business outcomes.

questions.question: An architect is tracing a data element through an OmniScript and finds it is fetched but never displayed or saved. What should be done?
options: Keep it in the fetch in case it is needed later
Remove it from the fetch to reduce waste
Move it to a separate Integration Procedure
Store it in a custom setting
questions.explanation: A data element that is fetched but never used is waste, and removing it from the fetch reduces bandwidth, memory, and query budget. Keeping it in case it is needed later is speculative and inefficient. Moving it to a separate IP adds a round trip for unused data. A custom setting is for configuration, not for unused fetched data.

questions.question: A save operation writes a record even when none of its fields changed. What is the best improvement?
options: Write the record anyway to keep it simple
Design the save to write only the records and fields that changed
Add more fields to the save so it is more complete
Move the save to a FlexCard
questions.explanation: Writing only what changed avoids redundant writes, which waste time and trigger unnecessary triggers and workflows. Writing anyway is the inefficiency being fixed. Adding more fields makes the problem worse. A FlexCard is a display component and does not perform saves.

questions.question: A complex transformation must produce identical results for three OmniScripts. Where should it live?
options: In a single shared Integration Procedure
In the browser's JavaScript for each script
In a custom label that stores the output
questions.explanation: A single shared Integration Procedure guarantees identical results and is written and tested once. Duplicating it in each script risks drift. Browser JavaScript duplicated per script has the same drift problem. A custom label stores text, not a transformation result.
